title: Researchers say hacker used DeepSeek-driven AI agent to steal residents’ data from a service provider for Flemish municipalities
date_note: Researchers’ findings were published 25 November 2026; the campaign ran from 6 to 15 November per the pages.
org: Service provider for Flemish municipalities (not named)
geo_basis: Flemish municipalities; the provider and municipalities are not named, Brussels used for Belgium
actor: Ghost Hunters (APT90), as named by Secutec and SOCRadar
summary: Secutec and SOCRadar say a hacker linked to Ghost Hunters (APT90) used the Chinese model DeepSeek to drive an autonomous agent built with Hermes Agent in a campaign called BabidiGhost, from 6 to 15 November. ITdaily reports the attacker reached a service provider’s server and took residents’ data. Computable says over a million residents and employees of Flemish municipalities were affected; neither page names the provider.
plain: Researchers say a hacker used an AI agent steered by DeepSeek to steal ID and personal data tied to Flemish municipalities from a service provider’s server.
exec: Researchers report municipal residents’ identity data stolen through a service provider, with an AI agent doing much of the work.
action: Secutec and SOCRadar say multi-factor authentication and IP restrictions held off the attacks; SOCRadar published detection rules and indicators for IT teams to search their logs.
impact: Stolen data includes names, addresses, birth dates, national register and ID card numbers and IBANs, according to ITdaily and Computable.

validation.note: ITdaily and Computable, two Belgian publishers, each report the Secutec/SOCRadar findings on the BabidiGhost campaign. The researchers’ own reports and any statement from the CCB or the municipalities were not read.
